animationInventory.statement: The authoritative deck contains no native PowerPoint timing, build, or transition elements and no GIF, audio, or video assets.

extractionPolicy: Every PPTX-embedded media file is preserved byte-for-byte in its original format. Only the public filename is made descriptive.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: The strategy-game definition says rules specify a reward for every move.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: Define terminal utility for completed outcomes and a cutoff evaluation function for nonterminal leaves; individual moves need not carry rewards.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: The deck describes minimax as maximizing my advantage and minimizing the opponent's advantage and says it is based on breadth-first search with a bound.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: Define minimax as choosing the action with the best worst-case backed-up utility against an optimal opponent; implement the recursive computation depth-first to terminal or cutoff states.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: The root is said to become MAX or MIN according to whether the heuristic is a reward or cost and the presenter note says it is unimportant which player moves first.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: The player to move and the fixed utility perspective determine whether the root is MAX or MIN. Utility signs must remain consistent throughout the tree.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: The deck broadly says to apply a heuristic only to leaf nodes without separating terminal leaves from depth-cutoff leaves.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: Use exact utility at terminal states and an evaluation function at nonterminal cutoff leaves; internal values are then backed up recursively.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: The presenter notes say a new game tree may have to be recreated after every opponent move.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: Advance the root to the observed child and reuse a matching subtree or transposition-table entries when valid; rebuild only the portions invalidated by the new state or search budget.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: The questions can imply minimax guarantees a win and may fail when an opponent makes a mistake.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: Minimax remains a safe optimal-opponent policy and can exploit a mistake if the new state is searched, but it guarantees a win only from a theoretically winning position under the modeled rules and search assumptions.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: The presenter note explains cutoff evaluation with the Machiavelli phrase end meets means and frames MIN as choosing the opponent's worst move.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: Remove the slogan. Explain that MIN chooses the action minimizing MAX's utility under a zero-sum convention, and that the cutoff evaluation approximates future terminal utility.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: Alpha-beta is said to use more informed heuristics while applying the heuristic to a state and all its siblings.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: Alpha-beta returns the same depth-limited minimax result without changing the evaluation function. Move-ordering heuristics improve pruning efficiency, and cutoff siblings are deliberately not evaluated.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: The slide labels are reversed relative to the standard cutoff names: Max-Value v greater than or equal to beta is labeled ALPHA cutoff, while Min-Value v less than or equal to alpha is labeled BETA cutoff.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: Use beta cutoff at a MAX node when v is greater than or equal to beta, and alpha cutoff at a MIN node when v is less than or equal to alpha.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: The presenter note says only examine branches greater than alpha or less than beta.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: Alpha and beta are path bounds, not prefilters. Examine children in order until a returned bound proves that remaining siblings cannot affect the ancestor decision.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: The final worked example announces a cutoff after the last child value two has already been evaluated.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: The condition beta less than or equal to alpha is true, but there are no remaining siblings to skip, so that particular cutoff saves no additional evaluation.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: The slide says alpha-beta never prunes a branch and instead does not expand unnecessary branches, and proposes checking current and parent heuristic values to verify correctness.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: Describe pruning as skipping the expansion or evaluation of remaining subtrees. Verify that alpha-beta and full minimax return the same root value and selected action at the same depth and evaluation function, while alpha-beta evaluates no more leaves.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: The bibliography misspells George F. Luger as George Fluger and Russell as Russel.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: Use George F. Luger and Stuart Russell while preserving the original editions and chapter references.
